q1: SELECT DISTINCT DEPT_NAME FROM COURSE WHERE CREDITS = (SELECT MAX(CREDITS) FROM COURSE)
q2: SELECT DISTINCT DEPT_NAME FROM COURSE AS C, (SELECT MAX(CREDITS) AS MAX_CREDITS FROM COURSE GROUP BY DEPT_NAME) AS A WHERE C.CREDITS = A.MAX_CREDITS
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT DEPT_NAME FROM COURSE WHERE CREDITS = (SELECT MAX(CREDITS) FROM COURSE)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT DEPT_NAME FROM COURSE AS C, (SELECT MAX(CREDITS) AS MAX_CREDITS FROM COURSE GROUP BY DEPT_NAME) AS A WHERE C.CREDITS = A.MAX_CREDITS
counterexample: INSERT INTO COURSE (COURSE_ID, TITLE, DEPT_NAME, CREDITS) VALUES (1, 101, 1, 4); INSERT INTO COURSE (COURSE_ID, TITLE, DEPT_NAME, CREDITS) VALUES (2, 102, 1, 3); INSERT INTO COURSE (COURSE_ID, TITLE, DEPT_NAME, CREDITS) VALUES (3, 103, 2, 5); INSERT INTO COURSE (COURSE_ID, TITLE, DEPT_NAME, CREDITS) VALUES (4, 104, 2, 4);
explanation: Q1 retrieves the department name(s) of courses that have the maximum credits across the entire COURSE table. Q2 retrieves the department name(s) for each course whose credits match the maximum credits per department. These are fundamentally different objectives, so they can produce different results.
counterexample_dsp: A database with courses from two departments having different max credits. Q1 will return the department with the global max credits, while Q2 will return the department for each course that has the max credits within its own department.
